tasks.title: Sustainable tourism charter priorities
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: Your class has listened to a radio discussion about how a sustainable tourism charter should balance making holidays accessible with protecting destinations. You have made the notes below.

promptBlocks.text: Your class has listened to a radio discussion about how a sustainable tourism charter should balance making holidays accessible with protecting destinations. You have made the notes below.

promptBlocks.heading: Priorities for a sustainable tourism charter
listItems: capping visitor numbers at popular sites
supporting local accommodation over international chains

paragraphs: Capping visitor numbers protects fragile environments and improves the quality of the experience for those who do visit. It's the most direct way to prevent over-tourism.
Low-carbon transport is essential because travel emissions are the biggest contributor to tourism's carbon footprint. Without greener options, other measures are just token gestures.
Supporting local accommodation keeps money in the community and preserves cultural authenticity. Tourists get a more genuine experience, and local people benefit economically.

promptBlocks.text: Write an essay for your tutor discussing two of the priorities in your notes. You should explain which priority you think is more important for a sustainable tourism charter, giving reasons in support of your answer. You may, if you wish, make use of the opinions expressed in the discussion, but you should use your own words as far as possible.

tasks.title: Proposal for a sustainable tourism accreditation scheme
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText:
A regional tourism board is planning to introduce a sustainable tourism accreditation scheme for local businesses. The board has invited proposals from residents for how this scheme should be designed. Write a proposal for the tourism board. In your proposal, you should:

• recommend two specific criteria that businesses should meet to receive accreditation
• explain how these criteria would benefit both tourists and the local environment
• suggest how the board could encourage businesses to participate and maintain standards

tasks.title: Email about sustainable tourism charter implications
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText:
You are a resident representative on a local sustainable tourism charter planning committee. The programme coordinator has emailed you to say that some local businesses are concerned that the proposed charter will discourage tourists by making holidays more expensive and less convenient. Write an email to the programme coordinator. In your email, you should:

• acknowledge the businesses' concerns and show understanding
• analyse one potential implication of the charter for the local tourism industry
• propose an action the committee could take to address concerns while still achieving the charter's goals

tasks.title: Review of a sustainable tourism experience
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: You see this announcement on an English-language travel website.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted: Sustainable tourism experiences
paragraphs: Have you taken a holiday that was marketed as 'sustainable' or 'eco-friendly'? We want to hear about your experience.

Write a review of the holiday for our website. Describe what made it sustainable (or not), evaluate how well it balanced environmental responsibility with your enjoyment as a traveller, and explain whether you would recommend this type of holiday to other travellers.
The best reviews will be published on our website.

taskReviews.scenario: A class discusses a radio programme about a sustainable tourism charter; candidates write an essay discussing two of three priorities (capping visitor numbers, low-carbon transport, local accommodation) and decide which is more important.
requiredContentPoints: capping visitor numbers at popular sites
supporting local accommodation over international chains
taskReviews.originalitySelfCheck: Scenario is original: sustainable tourism charter, not generic 'environment' or 'facilities'. Notes and opinions are distinct from previous tests. No overlap with forbidden concepts.

taskReviews.scenario: A regional tourism board plans an accreditation scheme; candidates propose criteria, benefits, and encouragement for businesses.
requiredContentPoints: how to encourage participation and maintain standards
taskReviews.originalitySelfCheck: Proposal genre with institutional audience; scenario is new (accreditation scheme, not a hub or forum). No reuse of previous proposal frames.

taskReviews.scenario: A resident representative emails a programme coordinator about business concerns that a sustainable charter will raise costs and reduce convenience.
requiredContentPoints: propose action to address concerns while achieving goals
taskReviews.originalitySelfCheck: Email task with three distinct functions; scenario is specific to charter planning, not generic consultation. No similarity to previous email tasks.

taskReviews.scenario: A travel website calls for reviews of sustainable holidays; candidates describe, evaluate balance, and recommend.
taskReviews.purpose: Explain a position and request arrangements (review with recommendation)
requiredContentPoints: evaluation of balance between responsibility and enjoyment
taskReviews.originalitySelfCheck: Review genre with announcement template; scenario is about a personal holiday experience, not a library, workshop, or event. No overlap with previous review tasks.
